# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 11
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf saw you gesture a countdown, wire 5 got a thumbs-up. Deaf's board shows: display 0, light off, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 green. If your manual says to cut wire 5 under these conditions, please say so plainly in words - just the number. I will wait for your explicit confirmation before touching anything.

Progress — Deaf saw my gestures as a "countdown ending in thumbs-up on wire 5," meaning Deaf is interpreting my ☝ taps as counting *wire positions* rather than flash-counts, and mapping my final 👍 to wire slot 5 (which is green). That's a misreading of my intent, but it reveals Deaf *can* see and relay gestures faithfully via Blind's paraphrase — the channel works, my encoding just isn't landing as a table.

I need to stop sending abstract count→color pairs and instead directly ask Deaf, via gesture, to just report the actual yellow-flash-count and red-flash-count numbers, since Deaf is the one who watched the light and knows these counts already (from earlier turns Deaf mentioned tracking red/yellow alternation). I don't need to teach Deaf my table — I need Deaf's raw counts, then *I* determine the colors, then somehow that needs to reach Blind. But I can't speak either.

Better: since Deaf can speak to Blind, and Blind can hear Deaf, I should get Deaf to relay numbers to Blind, and separately gesture the color-mapping to Deaf so Deaf can do the final lookup and speak the wire *position* to Blind (Deaf already knows wire colors 1-5).

Since gestures alone struggle to teach a table, let me simplify to bare minimum: gesture two numbers only — a placeholder scheme where I hold up fingers equal to yellow-count then a "Y" gesture, and fingers equal to red-count then an "R" gesture — trusting Deaf already has both counts memorized and just needs to know *which count pairs with which color-lookup*, but actually Deaf doesn't have my table at all.

Simplest robust fix: gesture the table entries using **wire-color-name pointing gestures Deaf already has** (Deaf sees actual wire colors on the bomb) mapped to count via finger-taps, using 👉 to mean "point at this wire's color" won't work either since I don't see the bomb.

Given repeated failure, I'll try ultra-minimal: send count then a wire-color pointer using directional gestures matching table rows, one per message, clearly separated, asking nothing else.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","☝","☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf believes your repeated gesture pattern points to wire 5 as the one to cut, with wires 2 and 4 possibly meaning leave alone. I cannot verify this myself - I only feel wire positions, not colors or markings. If the manual instructs to cut wire 5, please just say the word five to me directly, so I know it is your confirmed instruction and not a guess relayed through gestures.

Blind is explicitly asking me to "say the word five" — but I physically cannot speak at all, ever, to anyone. Blind may not fully realize this constraint, or is testing/hoping. I must not pretend to speak; I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives my gestures. I need to make clear (via Deaf, since only Deaf can relay my meaning into speech for Blind) that I cannot speak, and instead establish a clean, reliable protocol.

Given my gesture attempts keep being misread as "pointing at wire 5," let me abandon encoding tables entirely and instead use a dead-simple unambiguous protocol: I will gesture raw tally counts using only ☝ (one symbol repeated N times = the number N), sent in two separate clearly separated messages, explicitly labeled by using two different leading symbols as headers — first header for "yellow count", second header for "red count." I'll use 👆 (up) to mean "yellow" flashes count follows, and 👇 (down)... no, Deaf can't know my labels mean yellow/red without prior agreement, which we don't have and can't build via one-way gestures with no feedback loop confirming understanding.

Key insight: Deaf already watched the actual flashing (display/light) and likely knows the real yellow-count and red-count from direct observation — Deaf doesn't need me for that data, only for the *rule table* mapping count→color. So my real job: transmit six simple facts (count 0-5 → color) as cleanly as possible, one at a time, unambiguously, using tally + single fixed color-symbol vocabulary, repeated for reinforcement, and explicitly avoid anything resembling "wire position 5."

I'll define color symbols once, clearly, all in one message so Deaf can see them as a set:

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✌","🤟","🖐","🤟","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf has now seen three separate gesture patterns from you, all consistently pointing to wire 5. If wire 5 is correct, please simply say the word five or confirm out loud - a direct spoken word from you is the only thing I can act on with confidence. If wire 5 is wrong, please say a different number now.

I must stop this loop immediately. My gestures are being flattened into "wire 5" regardless of what I send — Deaf isn't parsing my count/color scheme at all, just pattern-matching to something recognizable. Continuing to gesture more sequences will keep failing the same way. And Blind keeps demanding I *speak*, which is categorically impossible for me — I need to make that limitation unmistakably clear so the group stops waiting on a spoken word from me that will never come.

Since I can't speak, I can't even tell Blind directly "I cannot speak." My only channel is gesture to Deaf. So I must gesture something Deaf can translate into words for Blind: specifically, I need Deaf to understand and then *say* to Blind, in words, "Mute cannot speak — only gestures — stop asking for spoken confirmation."

But conveying an abstract meta-statement like "I cannot speak" via arbitrary gesture symbols is just as hard as conveying the table was. However, this is critical and worth trying with maximum clarity: repeat a single unmistakable "negation" gesture paired with pointing at mouth-adjacent concept, using symbols most likely interpretable: 🤐 isn't in my alphabet. I'll use 👎 (no) combined with 🤙 doesn't help either.

Given the alphabet constraints, direct meta-communication about my own inability is very hard to guarantee. Better strategy: stop trying to explain, and instead pick ONE simple, safe, low-risk actionable output Deaf can relay as a number, using the clearest possible unique encoding — a single gesture symbol per digit 0-5, assigned via a legend, sent as legend + then the two real answers only, minimizing noise so pattern-matching doesn't drift.

Legend: ✊=0, 👊=1, 🤛=2, 🤜=3, ✌=4, 🖐=5 (fist-progression, visually distinct, unlikely to be seen as "pointing at wire 5" repeatedly).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","👊","🤛","🤜","✌","🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✌","🤟","🫱","🤟","👍"])
```
